Below are all the packages and data needed for this exercise:

```{r load and import}
library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(rio, here, flexdashboard,
       tidyverse,ggrepel, ggplot2,
       DT, knitr, png)

#data
cleaned_NHANES <- import(here("Data", "cleaned_NHANES.csv"))


```

# Setting up charts

    
Row {data-height=650}
-------------------------------------

### Age distribution figure.

```{r figure}
include_graphics(here("Figures", "age_plot.png"))
```

Row {data-height=350}
-------------------------------------
   
### Gauge indicating percentage of individuals 21 years or older.

```{r gauge, echo = FALSE}
# calculating percentage of individuals 21 years or older
percent_adults <- mean(cleaned_NHANES$age >= 21, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
gauge(percent_adults, min = 0, max = 100, symbol = '%', 
        gaugeSectors(
        success = c(0, 100), color = "steelblue"
          )
    )
```   


### ValueBox indicating percentage of individuals with average SBP > 120mm Hg.

```{r valueBox, echo = FALSE}
# Recreating average SBP

## creating one dataframe with all SBP values 
SBP_df <- data.frame (
  SBP1 = cleaned_NHANES$systolic_bp_1,
  SBP2 = cleaned_NHANES$systolic_bp_2,
  SBP3 = cleaned_NHANES$systolic_bp_3,
  SBP4 = cleaned_NHANES$systolic_bp_4
)

## making a SBP average, despite NA missing data
SBP_average <- rowMeans(SBP_df, na.rm = TRUE)

cleaned_NHANES <- cleaned_NHANES %>%
  mutate(
    SBP_average = SBP_average
  )
## Set SBP_mean to NA if all 4 values are missing
cleaned_NHANES$SBP_average[
  is.nan(cleaned_NHANES$SBP_average)] <- NA

## calculating percentage of individuals with SBP > 120 mm Hg
percent_high_avg_SBP <- mean(
  cleaned_NHANES$SBP_average >= 120, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
percent_high_avg_SBP <- round(percent_high_avg_SBP, digits = 2)

# creating value box with percentage above
valueBox(percent_high_avg_SBP)
```
